media.title: A Plastic Ocean
media.plot: Investigates the devastating impact of plastic pollution on marine life including sea turtles across the world's oceans.

media.title: Blue Planet II
media.plot: Features hawksbill turtles feeding among coral reefs and the threats facing their ocean habitat.

media.title: Turtle: The Incredible Journey
media.plot: Follows a loggerhead turtle on its extraordinary migration across the Atlantic, revealing the perilous life of sea turtles.

media.title: Mission Blue
media.plot: Oceanographer Sylvia Earle campaigns to protect marine ecosystems, highlighting species like the hawksbill turtle.

habitat.description: Hawksbill turtles frequent shallow coastal waters, particularly coral reefs, rocky areas, lagoons, and mangrove-lined estuaries. They are one of the most reef-associated of all sea turtles, using their narrow, pointed beaks to extract sponges from crevices. Nesting occurs on remote tropical beaches, often on small islands.

threats.name: Shell Trade
threats.description: Despite CITES bans, hawksbill shell ('tortoiseshell') is still trafficked for jewelry and ornamental objects, particularly in East Asia.

threats.name: Coral Reef Degradation
threats.description: Ocean warming, acidification, and pollution destroy the coral reef ecosystems hawksbills depend upon for food.

threats.name: Egg Harvesting
threats.description: Nesting beaches are raided for eggs in many tropical regions, reducing recruitment of young turtles.

threats.name: Bycatch
threats.description: Turtles are accidentally caught in fishing nets, longlines, and trawls, often drowning before they can be released.

culturalSignificance.overview: Sea turtles have navigated Earth's oceans for over 100 million years, surviving mass extinctions that claimed the dinosaurs. The hawksbill's beautiful shell has been coveted since antiquity - ancient Romans, Greeks, and Japanese all fashioned it into luxury items. Today it symbolizes the fragility of marine ecosystems.
literature: Voyage of the Turtle by Carl Safina
The Old Man and the Sea by Ernest Hemingway
Sea Turtles: A Complete Guide by James Spotila
culturalSignificance.symbolism: Represents ancient wisdom, ocean health, and the interconnection between coral reef ecosystems. Their decline signals the broader crisis facing marine environments.
